A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same STaRFormer work, with readable text, equations, figures, and tables across 15 pages. Both end with references; neither contains appendices. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original STaRFormer classification experiments on 15 datasets, component ablations, masking sensitivity experiments, and latent-space analyses in Section 4, Tables 1–7, and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original classification results, ablations, masking sensitivity experiments, and latent-space analyses in Section 4, Tables 1–7, and Figure 3.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the identical shared-parameter Transformer architecture, DAReM masking procedure, classification head, and fused batch-wise/class-wise contrastive objective.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same classification tasks on DKT, Geolife, PAM, and the same 12 UCR-UEA datasets. No dataset, domain, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in every corresponding comparison in Tables 1–4, including RNN/LSTM/GRU for DKT and the same PAM baselines such as Raindrop and ViTST.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the same evaluation metrics, data-split procedures, sample counts, and controlled ablation settings. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Both versions contain identical architecture/masking ablations, contrastive-loss component and weighting experiments, regional-mask sensitivity analysis, and t-SNE comparisons in Tables 5–7 and Figure 3.

E5.justification: The five-seed reporting for DKT and Geolife, five PAM splits, and standard-deviation reporting are unchanged. Geolife Table 1 continues to report the top score.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and rankings in Tables 1–7 and the qualitative findings in Section 4 and Figure 3 are identical. For example, PAM accuracy remains 97.6 ± 0.9% in Table 2.

T1.justification: Problem 1, the mathematical definitions, and Equations (1)–(6), covering attention aggregation, attention scores, and contrastive losses, are identical. No proofs or theoretical results are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contribution bullets, and conclusion retain identical claims about DAReM, semi-supervised contrastive learning, and performance across diverse sequential-data tasks.

C2.justification: Interpretations of masking, contrastive learning, and latent-space separation are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitation concerning quadratic attention cost for long sequences.

D1.justification: The disclosed hyperparameters, training hardware (16GB Tesla V100-SXM2), and experimental details are identical. Both abstracts retain the same promise that code and data will be made available.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 79 references are unchanged, as are the comparisons with prior approaches and the claimed research positioning.

P1.justification: Page 1 corrects the first author's given name from Maxmilian to Maximilian and changes his email domain from reserach.glasgow.ac.uk to research.gla.ac.uk. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; body wording and document structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–7 retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. The page design is retained, and pages 2–15 render pixel-identically.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the accuracy of the first-page author details, while the method, experimental evidence, explanations, limitations, and document organization remain identical. These limited corrections do not meaningfully change the paper's overall quality.
